name: Guerneville - River Weekend
region: Guerneville & the Russian River, Sonoma County, California
summary: A four-day Russian River weekend: redwoods, river paddling, and a genuinely good small-town food and bar scene, with the one real climb (Austin Creek's East Ridge, above the tourist-flat Armstrong loops) leading. The limiters: this is a working weekend, so mornings flex around a café work block; the river run needs early-season water levels; Johnson's Beach operates only June–Labor Day; and 2026 trail closures at Austin Creek must be re-verified at the kiosk. Expect the mellow counterpoint done well — ancient groves, a mid-float brewery beach-up, boon's 24 seats (reserve ahead), and show night at Monte Rio's quonset-hut theater.

activities.name: Austin Creek — East Ridge climb (above the redwoods)
activities.description: The earned pick, and the one almost no one does: everyone walks the flat, paved Armstrong redwood loops below — this climbs out of them. East Ridge Trail gains ~1,500 ft over 4 mi to Bullfrog Pond through oak woodland and open ridge with panoramic wilderness views, loopable back down Pool Ridge (steep upper section). 6,000 acres and usually empty. VERIFY before you go (2026): Gilliam Creek Trail is closed and Bullfrog Pond Campground is closed; East Ridge and Pool Ridge were open. Day use 8 AM–sunset, $10/vehicle, no water or restrooms up top, limited cell service, rattlesnakes in warm weather. Register/check status at the Armstrong kiosk.

activities.name: Burke's Canoe Trips — self-guided river run
activities.description: The on-profile river day: a ~10-mile self-guided canoe/kayak run from Burke's, put in 7.5 mi upstream and their crew shuttles you back to your car. Beach the boat at Stumptown Brewery mid-float for a beer. Go earlier in the season while river levels are high enough. A step up from renting a tube at the paid beach.

activities.name: Armstrong Redwoods — the ancient grove
activities.description: The accessible counterpoint — and here it's the point: an easy flat walk among 300-ft coast redwoods, the 1,400-year-old Colonel Armstrong tree and the 310-ft Parson Jones. Rivals Muir Woods with a fraction of the crowds. Free to walk in (pay to drive/park). Pair it as the mellow half of an Austin Creek day.

activities.name: boon eat + drink
activities.description: The town's standout: 24 seats, Sonoma-local seasonal cooking by chef-owner Crista Luedtke (who's largely behind Guerneville's food revival). Reserve ahead in season. This is the 'spend where it earns it' dinner.

activities.name: Coffee Bazaar — the work-morning café
activities.description: The café-work anchor for the working half of the weekend: eclectic 30-year spot attached to a bookstore, coffee, homemade baked goods and breakfast sandwiches. Downtown, walkable, reliable — the place to knock out a focused block before the river.

activities.name: El Barrio — cocktails
activities.description: The town's good cocktail bar — another Luedtke spot, small and lively. Closes early (~9 PM), so it's a pre-dinner drink, not a late night. The evening warm-up before boon or Trillium.

activities.name: Johnson's Beach afternoon swim
activities.description: The town beach since the 1920s: a calm, roped-off stretch of the Russian River a two-minute walk from Main Street, with beach and boat rentals 10:00–17:00 and a snack shack, free admission, $10 parking. It is the un-fancy local scene, not a resort. Verified caveats: beach operations run daily only June 1 to Labor Day, no outside alcohol, dogs banned on the beach; the lot closes at 18:00.

activities.name: Duncans Mills village afternoon
activities.description: A ten-minute drive downriver, this preserved railroad-era hamlet packs about 14 independent merchants — vinyl, antiques, a poetry bookshop, a proper general store with a full deli counter — into a few wooden blocks, with zero chain anything. Cap it with a flight at Sophie's Cellars, a local wine bar pouring limited-production Sonoma wines with artisan cheese: far better value than the tour-bus tasting rooms. Verified caveat: Sophie's Cellars is closed Tuesdays (otherwise open from noon); shop hours vary midweek — confirm ahead.

activities.name: Stumptown Brewery riverside deck
activities.description: Small in-house brewery a mile east of town with a big deck hanging over two acres of Russian River frontage — house beers plus guest taps, smoked brisket and pulled-pork sandwiches off the pub menu, dogs welcome. It is the locals' golden-hour porch, not a tasting-room production. Caveat: the official site was unreachable when checked and the 11:00–23:00 daily hours come from third-party listings — confirm ahead.

activities.name: Monte Rio Theater show night
activities.description: A movie or live show inside a Quonset-hut theater on the Bohemian Highway whose auditorium ceiling is draped with the largest surviving piece of Christo and Jeanne-Claude's Running Fence — community-run, with films, live music, and a free Open Mic Wednesdays (18:00–22:00, backline provided). Verified caveat: programming is event-based rather than nightly showtimes, so check the calendar before driving over.

pois.name: Armstrong kiosk (entrance + status check)
pois.description: Pay day use here and confirm current trail status — closures change. Same entrance as the redwood reserve.

pois.name: East Ridge Trailhead
pois.description: Trail leaves the reserve and climbs; you're under redwoods at first, then out onto open ridge.

pois.name: Bullfrog Pond (turnaround / loop point)
pois.description: Top of the climb. Pond often dry by mid-summer. Loop back via Pool Ridge for a different line down.

pois.name: Burke's Canoe Trips (put-in + shuttle)
pois.description: Forestville, at Mirabel Rd. Self-guided rentals with shuttle service; also riverside campsites.

pois.name: Stumptown Brewery (mid-float beer stop)
pois.description: Beach the boat and walk up. Farmhand deli next door is the better food call. Shared stop: mid-float on the paddle day, or the evening deck session.

pois.name: Colonel Armstrong Tree (~1,400 yrs)
pois.description: Oldest tree in the grove, on an easy loop near the entrance.

pois.name: Parson Jones Tree (310 ft)
pois.description: Tallest in the reserve — longer than a football field.

pois.name: Nimble & Finn's ice cream (dessert)
pois.description: Handmade ice cream a few steps away; open late Fri/Sat. The after-dinner cone.

pois.name: Rainbow Cattle Company
pois.description: Historic gay dive bar one block from the beach, open 365 days a year ('Come Hell or High Water'; from 14:00 weekends, 16:00 weekdays). A Guerneville institution and a natural post-swim beer stop. Widely reported as cash-only in recent reviews — confirm ahead; the official site does not state it.

pois.name: Sophie's Cellars
pois.description: Wine bar specializing in limited-production wines from across Sonoma County, paired with locally sourced cheeses. Open from noon daily except Tuesday.

pois.name: Duncans Mills General Store
pois.description: Working general store with a full-service deli counter — sandwiches and salads made to order, good picnic provisioning for the riverbank. Listed hours 08:00–20:00 daily via third-party directories — confirm ahead.

pois.name: Monte Rio Community Beach
pois.description: Big public beach under the Monte Rio bridge, a short walk from the theater — an easy golden-hour stop before an evening show. Free access; facilities are seasonal — confirm ahead.

pois.name: Redwood Forest Theater
pois.description: A stone-terraced amphitheater tucked into the grove, a short detour off the main trail and usually empty — one of the quietest spots in the reserve. State Parks lists it only for rare case-by-case event reservations, so expect it open to wander, not programmed.

pois.name: Mom's Beach (Forestville River Access)
pois.description: The locals' name for the county's Forestville River Access, a scenic rocky-shore beach minutes from Burke's launch — free parking, seasonal restrooms, and free loaner life vests in summer. The small lot fills on hot weekends and the gate closes when full; alcohol is banned on summer weekends and holidays.

pois.name: Vacation Beach summer dam crossing
pois.description: Old-school river hamlet downstream of Guerneville where a seasonal summer dam slows the river into a warm swimming hole — pure unpolished Russian River, no facilities, no fee. Confirm ahead: the dam is only installed in summer and neighborhood lane access/parking is tight.

pois.name: Guerneville Bridge (1922)
pois.description: A rare pin-connected Parker truss opened December 1922 and preserved as a pedestrian bridge since 1998 (National Register #89000945) — the best free mid-river view in town, steps from the beach. Foot and bike traffic only; cars use the modern Hwy 116 bridge beside it.

pois.name: Guerneville River Park
pois.description: Quiet 5.3-acre county day-use park at the south foot of the old bridge — lawns, picnic tables, walkways, and a non-motorized kayak/paddleboard launch, all with free parking; an easy post-café leg-stretch across the river. Open 07:00 to 30 minutes before sunset only.

pois.name: Guerneville Pee Wee Golf & Arcade
pois.description: Gloriously kitsch vintage mini-golf under hand-painted dinosaurs and giant figures on Drake Road, just over the bridge — adults $9, kids 5-and-under free, cheap and genuinely local fun before or after cocktails. Confirm ahead: the official site listed weekend-only 11:00–17:00 hours when checked, while directories claim daily hours.

pois.name: Northwood Golf Club
pois.description: A 1928 Alister MacKenzie-designed 9-holer threaded through old redwoods on the way to Monte Rio — one of the country's best-rated nine-hole courses, with green fees starting around $25, a fraction of destination-course prices. Confirm 2026 rates and tee times via the club.

pois.name: Duncans Mills Depot Museum & rail cars
pois.description: The 1907 Northwestern Pacific depot with restored narrow-gauge cars and the caboose from the last train out in 1935, sitting on the old tracks at the edge of the village. The museum interior keeps irregular hours — but the rail cars are outside and viewable anytime.
